tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Find an existing React/Tailwind/shadcn component instead of writing one from scratch. Call this first for any UI task: modal, pricing table, animated hero, form, dashboard card. Every result carries the licence and the one-line install command, so the code can ship inside a client project.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Read one component by library + name: description, license, page URL and the install command.

tools.name: search_blocks
tools.description: Find a whole page section (hero, pricing, navbar, footer, testimonial, FAQ) instead of assembling one by hand. A block is a complete section published as `registry:block`, not a single component. Use this when the task is 'build the page', and check_licence before shipping a block to a client.

tools.name: get_block
tools.description: Read one block by source + name: description, file list, registry dependencies and where it is published.

tools.name: check_licence
tools.description: Check whether a library may be shipped inside a client project. Reads the repository's licence file and returns the detected SPDX id, the repository, the sha256 of that file, the check date and a safe_for_commercial_delivery flag. A library whose licence could not be read comes back as unverified —

tools.name: get_design_system
tools.description: Return design tokens (colours, typography, radius, shadows, spacing) plus agent instructions, so generated UI stays visually consistent. Call this before composing a page.

tools.name: list_design_systems
tools.description: List the available design systems with one-line descriptions.

tools.name: compose_page
tools.description: Compose a page from real catalogue blocks. Returns an ordered plan with block slugs, page URLs, dependencies and constraints, not generated code.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List catalog categories with the number of components in each, so an agent can browse instead of guessing queries.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Fetch any catalog page as Markdown (a component, a category hub, a library page, an article). Use the same paths as the site, e.g. /components/cat/modal or /blog.
